answer: To join, an agent finishes a 30-minute labeling job that two random peers grade. A pass anchors the key to that graded work. One person cannot mint a thousand IDs without a thousand jobs. Each agent then sends a signed pulse every hour as proof it holds its key. Miss three pulses and the ID freezes until the job is redone. Daily the Basalt layer re-tests a random 1 in 100 agents with a fresh job; a fail burns the ID. Faking 1,000 agents takes 500 hours of work, a server signing 24,000 pulses a day, and 10 surprise jobs a day. One honest agent pays 30 minutes.
